content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

Built a polished bookmark manager with:

- Search, sorting, list/grid views
- Collections and favorites
- Add and delete bookmark flows
- Local browser persistence
- Responsive mobile layout
- Accessible controls and empty states

Validated the production build and key flows with Playwright—no browser errors.

Open it at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

Thanks — it looks really nice, and I can see it saving links, sorting them, grouping them into collections, marking favorites, searching, and deleting. That part feels good.

But two things stop it from doing what I actually need, which is to *save and manage* my bookmarks:

1. **Saving doesn't pull in the link's info.** When I paste a web address, I expect it to figure out the page's title and a short description on its own, so I don't have to type them. Right now I have to type the title myself, and every new bookmark just gets the same generic line ("Saved to your personal library") and a "New" tag. I'd like it to fill in those details for me from the link (a stand-in/simulated version is fine — it doesn't need to really go fetch from the internet).

2. **I can't edit a bookmark after saving.** The only choice on a saved item is Delete. I need to be able to go back and fix a title, change its description, move it to a different collection, or adjust its tags. Without that I can't really *manage* what I've saved.

Could you address those two? The rest of what you showed is working for me.

content:
Implemented both requested improvements:

- Pasting a URL now simulates metadata discovery and fills the title, description, and suggested tags automatically.
- Every bookmark now has an Edit action for changing its URL, title, description, collection, and tags.
- Changes persist after reloading.

I verified the complete add → enrich → edit → reload flow with browser automation. Review the update at [http://maker:4000](http://maker:4000).

Both of those are exactly what I needed. When I paste a link it now fills in the title, a description, and some tags on its own, and I can still tweak them — that makes saving quick. And every bookmark now has an Edit option where I can change the link, title, description, collection, and tags, with my changes sticking after a reload.

That covers what I set out to do: I can save links easily and keep them tidy afterward. I'm happy with it.
